use_case: Container and berth scheduling optimization: berth windows and crane splits, yard slot allocation and truck appointment slot allocation
vendor_or_model: In-house optimization with machine-learning predictions of move times, dwell and vessel arrival, on the Cloud provider B ML platform
data_categories: Vessel schedules, bay plans, container attributes (size, weight, reefer, hazardous class), yard inventory, equipment status, move history, appointments by trucking company ID (no driver identifiers)
affects_individuals: Yes (carriers and trucking companies; workers who execute plans)
human_in_the_loop: Planner approves every plan in the TOS; second planner for hazardous cargo; at T-01 the TOS constraint check blocks violating plans before they reach automated equipment
applicable_laws: N48-49-R01 (101.650(b)(3), (f)); 46 U.S.C. 41106 (Shipping Act); 29 CFR part 1917; Texas Responsible AI Governance Act (T-07 pilot; intent-based prohibitions)
status: In production (T-01, T-03, T-04); pilot (T-06, T-07)
subpart_f_designation: Critical IT (writes plans to the TOS staging area; at T-01 approved plans drive automated stacking cranes)
fairness_testing_status: Berth windows tested across carrier services (pass); appointment-slot fairness not tested (POAM-025)
monitoring: Monthly feasibility, constraint blocks, overrides and rehandles per terminal; quarterly fairness tests from 2026-Q4

use_case: Gate OCR reading container, chassis and license plate numbers
data_categories: Gate camera images; container and plate numbers
human_in_the_loop: Low-confidence reads and mismatches go to a gate clerk; release still requires hold and appointment checks
applicable_laws: N48-49-R01 (101.650(b)(3), (f)); state breach laws where gate records link a driver's name to identity numbers or location (the Florida definition of personal information in Fla. Stat. 501.171 includes government identity numbers and geolocation)
fairness_testing_status: Read accuracy by lane, lighting and plate state tracked; no individual-level decisions
monitoring: Weekly read-accuracy report; clerk override rate

use_case: Predictive maintenance for STS cranes and RTGs from drive, vibration and fault data
vendor_or_model: OEM analytics service plus in-house models
human_in_the_loop: Maintenance planners decide on every work order; the model never commands equipment
applicable_laws: N48-49-R01 (101.650(e)(3)(v), (f)(3)) for the telemetry connection; 29 CFR part 1917
subpart_f_designation: Interconnected with critical OT (one-way telemetry through the OT DMZ)
monitoring: Quarterly precision and recall against actual failures
